[ASSISTANT_SAID] Warrior poses can be challenging, especially in a dynamic flow class.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for improving balance and stability in warrior poses include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Foundation is key: Feet hip-width apart, front foot forward, back foot at a 90-degree angle.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Bend your front knee at a 90-degree angle, with the thigh parallel to the ground.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Lengthen your spine and avoid compression in the lower back.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Engage your core muscles to stabilize your body.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Keep your gaze forward, about 6-8 feet in front of you.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Use deep breaths to lengthen and ground yourself.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Practice warrior I, II, and III regularly.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Modify poses if feeling unsteady, such as bringing the back foot forward or using a block.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Focus on transitions into and out of warrior poses.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Seek feedback from Rachel or another instructor for personalized tips.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User is interested in tips for deepening forward bends.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for deepening forward bends include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Lengthen your spine before bending forward.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Engage your core to support your lower back.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Hinge at the hips instead of bending from the waist.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Keep knees slightly bent to relieve pressure on the lower back.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Use arms to deepen the forward bend by placing hands on the ground, blocks, or shins.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Breathe into the stretch, inhaling to lengthen and exhaling to deepen.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Relax shoulders to maintain a long neck.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Focus on stretching hip flexors
